Agent.text: Running the original was declined, so the window sizes stay estimated. Recording that:

I've built **Bojan Text**. I named it after you, using the name on your project folder; it shows in the title bar, the About box and the welcome page. It builds, starts, and passes Craft Anything's comparison check.

**What's in it**
- **Editor basics:** Sublime-style tabs, side bar, minimap, command palette, go-to-anything, find and replace, and a status bar. Unsaved text is kept between runs, like the original.
- **Theming:** the whole window now follows the chosen color scheme. A Theme & Appearance window adds accent color, roundness, spacing, tab style and font sizes. There are four new color schemes (Bojan Night is the default), and your installed Sublime schemes, such as Mariana, Monokai and Nord, show up as well.
- **Colorizer:** it recognizes hex, rgb/hsl/hwb, lab/oklch, 0x… codes, color calls written in code and named colors. Each code is filled with its own color, with a dot in the margin. Alt+Click opens a color picker that rewrites the code in place.
- **Markdown:**
  - Alt+M shows a live preview beside the text as you type; full-screen preview is also available.
  - Alt+B opens the preview in your browser, and the page refreshes itself as you type.
  - You can export to HTML.
- **Sublime packages:** it reads language definitions straight from your installed Sublime. 208 of 209 load, including JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, PHP and SQL. Sublime's Python plugins (like its LSP or Emmet packages) can't run outside Sublime. Instead the editor has its own language-server connection, which shows errors and hover info and has F12 go-to-definition. It also reads the servers you set up for Sublime's LSP package.

**What differs or is still unknown**
- **Window measurements are estimates.** You declined running the original, so the tab bar, side bar and minimap sizes are my guesses.
- **Features left out:**
  - There's no multi-cursor editing, because the toolkit's text box doesn't support it.
  - Screen-reader support is off.
  - The language-server part is untested here, because no language servers are installed on this PC.
- **The first launch takes about half a minute to load the Sublime languages.** After that it uses a saved copy and starts quickly.
- **I had to change the build setup.** This PC doesn't have Microsoft's C++ build tools, which Rust normally uses on Windows. I installed Rust's GNU toolchain for your user account (no admin needed) plus Rust's bundled LLVM tools, and pinned the project to them. I also switched to the simpler OpenGL graphics mode, because the default one crashed on this machine.
- **There's a leftover test folder inside the project's tools folder.** I couldn't remove it automatically and it's safe to delete.

A good next step would be to install one language server you use, such as rust-analyzer or pyright, so I can check that error underlines and hover info work. Or ask for multi-cursor editing.
